subject: sociology

source.track: IGCSE · ages 14–16 · Paper 1 (all three topics compulsory) plus Paper 2 (two of the three topics)

note: Units follow the syllabus's six numbered topics in teaching order. Paper 1's Research methods, Identity and Social stratification are compulsory; for Paper 2 candidates study two of Family, Education and Crime, and the atlas tracks all three so learners can follow whichever pair their school offers.

program.section: Paper 1 — Research Methods, Identity and Inequality
program.title: Research methods
topics: 1.1 How do sociologists approach the study of society?
1.2 What types of data and evidence do sociologists use?

program.section: Paper 1 — Research Methods, Identity and Inequality
program.title: Identity: self and society
topics: 2.1 How do we learn our identity?

program.section: Paper 1 — Research Methods, Identity and Inequality
program.title: Social stratification and inequality
topics: 3.2 What attempts have been made to reduce social inequalities?
3.3 How has globalisation affected inequalities between societies?

program.title: Family
topics: 4.1 What are the different types of families?
4.2 What is the role of the family for the individual and society?

program.title: Education
topics: 5.2 What are the roles and functions of education?
5.3 What factors help to explain differences in educational achievement and experience?

program.title: Crime, deviance and social control
topics: 6.1 What are crime, deviance and social control?
